zh.summary: DNS 像網路聯絡簿：查名稱、找位址，也查看郵件與名稱伺服器的設定。把查到的設定和服務實際運作分開，就能寫出清楚的盤點紀錄。

sourceBody.text: CEH M04-02｜DNS 列舉（DNS Enumeration）
零基礎資訊工程教學｜2026 年 10 月 23 日｜約 25–35 分鐘
今天最重要的觀念：DNS 幫助我們找到網路服務的相關資訊，但查得到資訊，不代表能夠連線、登入或取得使用權限。
我們從零開始，不只背 CEH 考試會出現的名詞，也要理解 DNS 為什麼存在、電腦如何使用它，以及資安工程師為什麼需要列舉 DNS 資料。
學完這一課，你應該能夠：
1. 解釋 DNS 如何協助電腦找到網站。
2. 認識 A、AAAA、CNAME、MX、NS、TXT、SOA、PTR 記錄。
3. 使用 dig、nslookup 查詢 DNS。
4. 辨識 NXDOMAIN、NODATA、SERVFAIL 與 Timeout。
5. 理解 AXFR、DNSSEC 與 DNS 資訊外洩的關聯。
一、從第一原理開始：為什麼需要 DNS？
假設你要進入一個網站：
https://www.example.com
人類容易記住 www.example.com，但電腦在進行網路通訊時，通常需要知道對方的 IP 位址。
這裡出現兩種不同的資訊：

rows: 查詢網域相關記錄的系統

sourceBody.text: 上述 IP 為保留的文件示範位址，不代表 example.com 的真實 IP。
DNS 就像通訊錄，但更準確地說，它是一套分散式資料查詢系統
假設你只知道朋友的姓名，想要打電話給他。
你會先查通訊錄，找到電話號碼，再撥打電話。
DNS 的基本概念也一樣：
請注意：DNS 查詢成功，只代表名稱解析這一步取得了結果，不代表網站一定能開啟。
即使取得 IP，後續仍可能遇到：

items: HTTPS 或 TLS 設定錯誤。
網站回覆 HTTP 403（禁止存取）。

sourceBody.text: 因此，你必須先建立一個資訊工程的重要觀念：
查詢名稱、建立網路連線、存取應用程式、取得權限，是不同階段的工作。
二、DNS 是怎麼運作的？
DNS 並不是由一台巨大的全球伺服器，儲存所有網站的名稱與 IP。
它是一個具有層級結構的分散式系統（Distributed System）。
想像你問學校行政人員：「某位教授的辦公室在哪裡？」
行政人員可能先確認學院，再詢問系所，最後找到辦公室。DNS 也有類似的分工。
我們分別理解這些角色。
1. Recursive Resolver（遞迴解析器）
這是替電腦尋找答案的服務。
你問：「www.example.com 的 IP 是多少？」
遞迴解析器負責向其他 DNS 伺服器查詢，或直接使用已經快取的答案。
例如 Cloudflare 提供的公開遞迴解析器 1.1.1.1。
2. Root Nameserver（根名稱伺服器）
它不需要知道每個網站的 IP，而是協助指出頂級網域的管理位置。
例如：「想找 .com，你可以往這個方向查。」
3. TLD Nameserver（頂級網域名稱伺服器）
TLD 是 Top-Level Domain。
例如 .com、.org、.tw。
它協助指出特定網域的權威名稱伺服器。
4. Authoritative Nameserver（權威名稱伺服器）
它負責回答自己所管理 DNS 區域的正式資料。
例如提供 www.example.com 的 A 記錄，或 example.com 的 MX 記錄。
這也是我們進行 DNS 列舉時，特別需要理解的角色。
[Cloudflare：DNS 伺服器角色](https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/dns/dns-server-types/)
為什麼要區分遞迴解析器與權威伺服器？
因為它們的責任不同。

rows: 提供自己所管理區域的正式資料
不以替一般使用者快取外部查詢為主要職責
其他 DNS 解析器及查詢用戶端
遞迴存取控制、快取安全
DNS 記錄管理、區域傳送、設定正確性

sourceBody.text: 這是本章第一個需要真正理解，而不只是記憶的核心觀念。
三、DNS 記錄：一份聯絡簿有不同欄位
DNS 不是只有「網域名稱對應 IP」這一種功能。
它使用不同類型的 Resource Record（資源記錄，簡稱 RR），分別儲存不同用途的資料。
你可以想像這是一個資料庫，當你查詢時，要指定自己想取得哪一種類型的資料。
以下全部使用虛構的 example.test 實驗網域，並非真實查詢結果。

rows: 一個名稱指向另一個名稱
指定網域的收信伺服器
管理 DNS 區域的基本資訊
由 IP 位址反查名稱

sourceBody.text: 這幾種記錄在 CEH 與實際網路管理中都很重要。
[Cloudflare DNS 記錄類型](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/reference/dns-record-types/)
3.1 A 與 AAAA：找到 IP 位址
A 記錄：
www.example.test.  A  192.0.2.10
表示 DNS 將這個名稱對應到一個 IPv4 位址。
AAAA 記錄：
www.example.test.  AAAA  2001:db8::10
表示名稱對應到 IPv6 位址。
兩個記錄可能同時存在，也可能只有其中一個。
請注意：一個名稱也可能對應到多個 IP，供負載平衡等用途。DNS 查到的 IP 也可能是 CDN 或反向代理伺服器，而不是真正的後端主機。
3.2 CNAME：替網站建立別名
假設一家公司有：
如果設定：
shop.example.test.  CNAME  www.example.test.
就表示 shop 是指向 www 的別名。
當程式需要找到 shop 的 IP，就可能沿著 CNAME 指向的名稱繼續解析。
但 CNAME 不是 HTTP 重新導向。它是 DNS 名稱之間的對應關係，並不代表瀏覽器網址列一定會改變。
3.3 MX：郵件應該送給誰？
MX 是 Mail Exchange。
例如：
example.test. MX 10 mail.example.test.
意思是：「寄往 @example.test 的郵件，應依 MX 記錄嘗試交給 mail.example.test 處理。」
這裡有三個需要分清楚的部分：

items: 10：MX 優先順序，數字越小，優先程度越高。

sourceBody.text: MX 告訴你郵件服務的入口，不會直接列出公司的員工信箱或個人帳號。
3.4 NS 與 SOA：誰負責管理 DNS？
NS 是 Name Server。
它指出某個 DNS 區域由哪些權威名稱伺服器負責。
SOA 是 Start of Authority。
它包含區域管理與同步相關資料，例如：

items: 負責聯絡人的電子郵件資訊（以 DNS 格式編碼）。

sourceBody.text: 這裡要學會另外一個詞：Zone（DNS 區域）。
一個 Zone 是由特定權威名稱伺服器負責的一組 DNS 資料。
它不一定涵蓋整個網域樹。例如 dept.example.test 可以獨立委派出去，成為另一個管理區域。
所以「取得一個 Zone 的全部資料」不等於「取得整個公司所有網域的資料」。
3.5 TXT 與 PTR
TXT 記錄能放置文字，例如網域擁有權驗證資訊或 SPF 郵件寄送政策。
PTR 則用於 Reverse DNS（反向 DNS 查詢）。
一般 DNS 查詢：
名稱 → IP
反向 DNS：
IP → 名稱
但有 PTR 並不代表反查得到的名稱一定具有相同的正向 A／AAAA 記錄，更不代表已驗證主機或使用者的身分。
正向與反向記錄必須交叉核對。
四、什麼是 DNS 列舉？為什麼資安工程師要學？
現在我們來到 CEH M04 的真正主題。
Enumeration（列舉），就是透過特定服務提供的查詢介面，收集更具體的資訊。
在 DNS 的情境中，我們是在整理網域與相關記錄，建立一份可以檢查的網路資產清單。
假設你是公司的資安工程師，要盤點自己管理的網域。
你可能希望知道：

rows: 公司網站指向哪些 IP？
是否發布 SPF 等郵件政策？
權威 DNS 是否設定異常？
某個 IP 有沒有反向名稱？

sourceBody.text: 但是要注意：DNS 列舉不是保證列出所有子網域的神奇指令。
通常要結合已知名稱清單、資產管理紀錄、合法的公開資訊，以及其他獲得授權的查核方式，才能建立較完整的盤點結果。
五、實際操作：使用 dig 查詢 DNS
這是本章最值得動手練習的部分。
我們使用 Linux 的 dig 工具，它的主要用途就是向 DNS 伺服器提出查詢、觀察回應。
[ISC BIND dig 文件](https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/stable/manpages.html#dig-dns-lookup-utility)
步驟一：確認 dig 是否存在
如果你使用 Ubuntu，可以開啟 Terminal（終端機），輸入：
dig -v
如果出現版本資訊，代表已經可以使用。
如果尚未安裝，在一般 Ubuntu 系統可以使用：

sudo apt update
sudo apt install bind9-dnsutils
步驟二：進行第一筆查詢
使用公開的文件範例網域 example.com：
dig example.com A
這段指令可以拆成：

rows: 指定查詢 IPv4 位址記錄

sourceBody.text: 為了理解輸出，我們先看一份虛構的實驗室查詢回應，不是 example.com 的實際結果。

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR

;; QUESTION SECTION:
;www.example.test.   IN  A

;; ANSWER SECTION:
www.example.test.  300  IN  A  192.0.2.10

;; SERVER: 192.0.2.53#53
請逐項閱讀。
QUESTION SECTION 告訴我們：這次問了什麼問題。
ANSWER SECTION 告訴我們：伺服器回答了什麼資料。
其中：
www.example.test.  300  IN  A  192.0.2.10
可以拆成五部分：

rows: 回應中的快取剩餘有效時間，單位秒

sourceBody.text: TTL 是 Time to Live，中文可稱「存活時間」或「快取有效時間」。
它告訴快取系統，這份資料在正常情況下可以保留多久。它不是網站能正常運作多久，也不是連線會維持多久。
步驟三：依序查詢不同類型
下面的指令可以複製到自己的 Linux 終端機執行。
Linux：DNS 基礎查詢練習

# IPv4
dig example.com A

# IPv6
dig example.com AAAA

# 權威名稱伺服器
dig example.com NS

# 收信伺服器
dig example.com MX

# 文字記錄
dig example.com TXT

# 區域管理資料
dig example.com SOA

# 反向查詢
dig -x 1.1.1.1
最後一個 -x 代表反向查詢。記得：這些指令取得的是查詢當下的 DNS 回覆，並非永久不變的設定。
步驟四：指定向哪一台 DNS 伺服器查詢
dig @1.1.1.1 example.com A
@1.1.1.1 的意思是指定向 Cloudflare 的公開遞迴解析器提出查詢，而不是使用 dig 預設的 DNS 伺服器。
你也可以使用：
dig @1.1.1.1 example.com A +noall +answer
這裡的：
這樣比較容易閱讀，但如果你正在調查 NXDOMAIN、NODATA 或 SERVFAIL，不要只看精簡輸出，因為狀態碼與其他重要資訊可能被隱藏。
如果使用 Windows 呢？
可以使用 PowerShell：
Resolve-DnsName -Name example.com -Type A
也可以使用 nslookup：

nslookup -type=A example.com
nslookup -type=MX example.com
這些工具的目的相同，主要差別在查詢語法與輸出的詳細程度。
六、DNS 查詢失敗：如何判斷發生什麼事？
這部分是 CEH 考試與實務故障排除的高優先重點。
我們需要把「查不到 IP」拆成不同原因。

rows: DNS 查詢沒有回報 DNS 錯誤
不代表一定有你要的記錄
查詢結果指出該名稱不存在
不代表整個網域的所有服務不存在
名稱存在，但沒有符合查詢類型的資料
DNS 伺服器無法成功處理查詢
在等待時間內沒有收到回覆
不一定是 DNS 伺服器當機

sourceBody.text: NODATA 不是獨立的 DNS 回應碼。常見情況是 NOERROR，但沒有符合所查類型的答案；RFC 2308 對此有明確定義。
[RFC 2308：傳統 NODATA 與否定快取](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308)

技術補充（與原稿分開）：上文依 RFC 2308 的傳統 NODATA 語意說明。RFC 9824 的 Compact Denial of Existence 允許權威伺服器對實際不存在的名稱合成 NODATA，因此在這類部署中，NODATA 不能單獨證明名稱存在。空白 Answer 也可能是 referral，應連同 Authority 與完整回應判讀；若有 CNAME 鏈，NXDOMAIN 可能指向最終目標。原稿題目保留作為傳統情境練習。[RFC 2308 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308.html#section-2) · [RFC 9824](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9824.html)
案例一：有 IPv4，沒有 IPv6
假設同一個名稱：
www.example.test
查詢 A：

status: NOERROR

www.example.test. A 192.0.2.10
查詢 AAAA：

status: NOERROR

ANSWER SECTION: empty
若完整回應確認屬於 NODATA，就表示名稱存在，但沒有取得所查詢的 AAAA 記錄。
這不等於網域不存在，更不等於網站完全無法使用。
案例二：SERVFAIL
假設 DNS 回覆：
status: SERVFAIL
可能原因包括權威伺服器問題、DNSSEC 驗證失敗、解析路徑異常等。
這時合理的調查方向是檢查不同解析器的回應、權威伺服器及相關 DNS 設定，而不是直接認定「網站被關閉」。
案例三：為什麼兩個人會查到不同結果？
即使查詢相同名稱，DNS 結果也可能不同。
常見原因包括：

items: 使用不同 DNS 解析器，快取內容尚未更新。
DNS 設定剛修改，TTL 尚未到期。
內部 DNS 與外部 DNS 提供不同記錄（Split-Horizon DNS）。
地理位置、負載平衡或 CDN 策略造成不同回覆。

sourceBody.text: 因此，資安調查必須記錄查詢的時間、伺服器、名稱、記錄類型及完整回應。
七、一般 DNS 查詢與 AXFR 有什麼差別？
AXFR 是 DNS Zone Transfer（DNS 區域傳送）的一種機制。
它本來就是正常的 DNS 管理功能，主要用於伺服器之間同步區域資料。
為什麼 AXFR 可能造成資安問題？
假設一個公司將大量內部系統名稱放入某個 DNS 區域：

www.example.test
mail.example.test
vpn.example.test
dev.example.test
backup.example.test
如果未經適當限制就對外提供整區傳送，可能讓沒有授權的人大量取得公司的系統名稱。
這些名稱不代表系統一定存在、可由外網連線或具有漏洞，但可能揭露不必要的架構資訊。
資安管理者應該限制區域傳送對象，必要時使用 TSIG 等驗證機制。AXFR 使用 TCP 傳輸；RFC 5936 也明確討論區域傳送存取控制。
[RFC 5936：AXFR](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936)
CEH 考試要記住的核心：AXFR 本身不是攻擊，而是一個可能因設定不當而造成資訊揭露的正常管理功能。
進行 AXFR 測試之前，應另行確認明確授權；能公開查詢某些 DNS 記錄，不表示已取得測試整區傳送的授權。
八、DNSSEC、Cache Snooping 與進階安全概念
這裡先建立正確的基本觀念，不需要馬上研究密碼學細節。
8.1 DNSSEC 是什麼？
DNSSEC 是 DNS Security Extensions。
它的主要目的，是讓驗證端能夠利用數位簽章驗證 DNS 資料的來源與完整性，降低遭到偽造或竄改的風險。
但它不是用來加密 DNS 查詢內容，也不負責授予網站存取權限。
[RFC 4033：DNSSEC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033)

rows: DNS 資料是否可驗證其來源與完整性
加密用戶端與 DNS 解析器之間的 DNS 通訊
透過 TLS 保護 DNS 通訊
保護瀏覽器與網站服務之間的 HTTP 通訊

sourceBody.text: 傳統 DNS 常使用 UDP 或 TCP 的 53 埠；DoH 常透過 HTTPS 的 443 埠，DoT 一般使用 853 埠。
不要將 DNSSEC 與 HTTPS 混為一談，它們處理不同層面的安全問題。
8.2 DNSSEC 的 NSEC 與名稱列舉
DNSSEC 需要有辦法驗證「某筆 DNS 記錄不存在」這種否定答案。
傳統 NSEC 會提供已存在名稱之間的資訊，某些實作可能讓外部觀察者沿著這些線索推得區域中的其他名稱，這稱為 Zone Walking。
但不是所有使用 NSEC 的系統都必然暴露完整名稱清單。現代也有 Compact Denial of Existence 等方式降低此類資訊揭露。
[RFC 9824：Compact Denial of Existence](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9824.html)
8.3 Cache Snooping 是什麼？
假設很多人共用一台 DNS 遞迴解析器。
如果外部觀察者可以利用某些查詢行為判斷解析器是否快取特定名稱，就可能推測該名稱曾經被查詢過。
這種技術稱為 DNS Cache Snooping。
不過，快取裡有某個名稱，不等於可以證明是哪一位使用者造訪了那個網站。快取可能來自其他使用者、預先查詢或其他系統行為。
防護上應限制誰能使用遞迴查詢及快取查詢功能，並避免不必要地對外開放。
九、把 DNS 放回完整資訊工程架構
這是我認為比單純準備 CEH 更值得掌握的觀念：你要知道 DNS 位於整個系統中的什麼位置。
當使用者要打開網站時，可以將問題拆成幾個階段。

rows: 服務名稱對應什麼資料？
能否連上目標 IP 與連接埠？
網站是否正確處理請求？
使用者能看見或修改什麼？

sourceBody.text: 你可以用下面的兩個指令體會差別：
dig example.com A
這是在查 DNS。
curl -I https://example.com
這是在嘗試以 HTTPS 對網站提出 HTTP HEAD 請求。
第二個指令涉及 DNS、網路連線、TLS、HTTP 等多個步驟，因此可以取得比單純 DNS 查詢更多的資訊。不過，有些網站不支援 HEAD 或對它設有限制，所以單次 curl -I 的結果也不能代表所有網站功能是否正常。
一位工程師要學會的是：先確認每個觀察結果屬於哪一層，再判斷下一步要測試什麼。
十、CEH M04-02 學習優先順序

rows: 理解其他所有概念的基礎
具備實際查詢與判讀能力
進一步理解管理與調查

sourceBody.text: P0／P1／P2 是本課建議的教學優先順序，不是 EC-Council 公布的正式題目比重。
十一、理解測驗：先自己作答
Q1. DNS 查詢獲得一個 A 記錄，最合理的結論是？
A. 已證明網站可以正常開啟
B. 已取得某個名稱對應的 IPv4 位址
C. 已確認網站的登入權限
D. 已取得伺服器管理權限
Q2. 查詢某名稱的 AAAA 記錄得到 NODATA，最合適的解讀是？
A. 這個網域必定不存在
B. DNS 伺服器一定當機
C. 該名稱存在，但沒有符合本次查詢類型的資料
D. 這個網站已被入侵
Q3. 為什麼 AXFR 需要存取控制？
A. 因為任何 DNS 查詢都會修改資料
B. 因為 AXFR 可能傳送整個區域的資料
C. 因為它能直接取得使用者密碼
D. 因為它會自動開啟網站管理介面
Q4. DNSSEC 的核心安全功能是哪一項？
A. 隱藏所有 DNS 名稱
B. 加密所有網站的 HTTPS 流量
C. 驗證 DNS 資料來源與完整性
D. 阻止任何人查詢公開的 A 記錄
Q5. 實務情境題
你在同一台 DNS 解析器上查詢 www.example.test，得到：

A    → 192.0.2.10
AAAA → NODATA
請用自己的話說明兩件事：
1. 目前可以確認什麼？不能確認什麼？
2. 如果想知道網站能不能正常開啟，接下來應該檢查什麼？
你現在不需要背下所有 RFC 或 DNS 指令參數。優先完成一次實際 DNS 查詢，能解釋查詢問題、回傳資料、TTL 與回應狀態的意義，再進入下一個 CEH 概念。

en.summary: DNS works like a network address book. It tells you about names, addresses, and mail or name servers. Keep those settings separate from tests of whether a service actually works.

sections.heading: 1. You found the address. What should you check next?
paragraphs: An address book can tell you where a store is. Checking whether it is open takes another step. DNS works much the same way: it returns data about a name. Website availability and sign-in permissions need their own checks.
The example below is made-up lab data, not a query we ran. example.test is an example name and 192.0.2.10 is a documentation address. Use your authorized lab data when practicing.

A domain name, such as www.example.test, is a name people can remember. An IP address is used for network communication. DNS is a distributed lookup system: different operators maintain different portions of its data.
Practice explaining who handles a lookup, choosing a record type, reading the full reply, and keeping DNS settings separate from website tests.

blocks.heading: Read three settings first
paragraphs: A gives the IPv4 address for www. CNAME makes shop an alias for www. MX names mail as a mail server; 10 is its preference value, with lower numbers preferred.
Record these as DNS settings. Test web access, mail delivery, and administrative rights separately within the agreed boundaries.
blocks.code:
www.example.test.   A       192.0.2.10
shop.example.test.  CNAME   www.example.test.
example.test.       MX      10 mail.example.test.

sections.heading: 2. Who looks up the answer? Who maintains it?
paragraphs: DNS enumeration means querying different record types and organizing the names, addresses, and server clues you receive. Record who you asked and when so you can compare results.

A recursive resolver looks up answers for you and may cache them. An authoritative server maintains the official data for a zone. A zone is a portion of DNS data managed by a set of authoritative servers; it may cover only part of a domain.

Traditional DNS uses UDP or TCP port 53. TCP also carries ordinary queries. Other DNS transports may be used in a particular environment. [DNS concepts](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034) · [Messages and records](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035)

Root servers help locate top-level domains such as .com, .org, and .tw. They are not a master list of website IP addresses. Recursive and authoritative describe roles; a server’s configuration determines which roles it provides.

blocks.caption: How does a resolver find an answer?
blocks.description: A simplified public DNS lookup. Cached answers or forwarding can change this path. Our example.test zone must be configured in a lab; public root servers will not lead you to this lesson’s data.

items.title: Your computer
items.body: Asks a recursive resolver for a name and record type.

items.title: Recursive resolver
items.body: Checks its cache, then asks other servers if needed.

items.title: Root and top-level domain (TLD)
items.body: The root points toward a TLD; the TLD supplies the relevant delegation.

items.title: Authoritative server
items.body: Answers for its zone. The resolver returns the result and caches it as allowed.

blocks.caption: Four things to keep with a lookup
blocks.description: This is a guide to reading a response. An answer may come from cache, or you may need another query.

items.title: Choose the target
items.body: Record the DNS server, name, and record type.

items.title: Read the response
items.body: Check the status, then the Answer and Authority sections.

items.title: Record the setting
items.body: Save the returned address, alias, or other fields.

items.title: Test services separately
items.body: Check web access, mail delivery, and sign-in rights separately.

sections.heading: 3. Which field answers your question?
paragraphs: A name can have several record types. Choose the type that answers your question. A asks for IPv4 addresses; AAAA asks for IPv6 addresses. [AAAA specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3596)
Start with known names, asset inventories, and approved sources. A record query answers the question you asked; a fuller inventory also requires other names and management records.

blocks.caption: Common DNS record types
rows: IPv4 / IPv6 addresses for a name.
An alias pointing to another name; follow that name to continue.
Mail server hostnames and preference values, rather than personal mailboxes.
Authoritative name servers for a zone.
Text such as domain verification data or mail policy.
Zone management data, including a serial number and synchronization timers.
A name for a reverse IP lookup; cross-check it with forward records.

blocks.heading: Connect the records to one example
paragraphs: One name may have several A or AAAA records. An address may belong to a CDN or reverse proxy; use asset records to identify the backend.

The CNAME for shop tells resolution to continue with www. It is a DNS alias, unlike an HTTP redirect that can change the browser’s URL. The MX value 10 is a mail-server preference; lower values come first. Mailbox accounts are managed separately.
blocks.code:
www.example.test.   A      192.0.2.10
www.example.test.   AAAA   2001:db8::10
shop.example.test.  CNAME  www.example.test.
example.test.       MX     10 mail.example.test.

blocks.heading: Optional: zones, SOA, and reverse lookups
paragraphs: For example, dept.example.test can be delegated to another operator as its own zone. The parent keeps delegation information; the child zone maintains its complete data.

SOA includes a primary name server, a contact mailbox encoded in DNS form, a serial number, and synchronization timers such as refresh and retry. TXT can carry domain-verification data or SPF mail policy.

A PTR record points to a name in reverse DNS. Look up that name’s A or AAAA records to compare the forward and reverse settings. Agreement is a configuration clue; identity authentication is a separate process. The IPv6 example 2001:db8::10 uses the documentation range. [IPv6 documentation addresses](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3849)

sections.heading: 4. What does an empty answer mean?
paragraphs: Read the whole response before deciding what is missing. NOERROR is a response status. An empty Answer section still requires a look at Authority and any aliases: the response may mean that the requested data is absent, or it may point you to another server.

SERVFAIL can result from authoritative-server trouble, a resolution-path problem, or DNSSEC validation failure. Within your authorization, compare resolvers and inspect configuration and logs. For a timeout, first record that no reply arrived during the wait, then investigate the network and server.

blocks.caption: Responses and useful notes
rows: The response code reports no DNS processing error. Read the contents to distinguish an answer, referral, or missing data.
The response says a name does not exist. With a CNAME chain, check which name it refers to.
Ordinary NODATA means the name exists but has no data of the requested type. Confirm the full reply; see the DNSSEC exception below.
The server had a problem completing resolution. Save the response and investigate.
No response arrived within the wait period. The cause still needs investigation.

blocks.heading: Optional: an empty NOERROR answer may be a referral
paragraphs: NODATA often appears as NOERROR without an answer of the requested type. An SOA in Authority and the rest of the response help you identify it. A referral may instead list NS records for servers to ask next.
Check the status, Answer, Authority, alias chain, and server together. Sometimes another query is needed to tell which situation applies. [RFC 2308](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2308)

blocks.heading: Why can the same name return different answers?
paragraphs: TTL is the caching lifetime advertised for a record, in seconds. A cached reply normally shows the remaining lifetime; an authoritative reply normally shows the configured value. Cache state, internal/external views (split-horizon DNS), CDN or geographic policy, and the server you ask can change the answer. TTL describes caching, not website uptime.
Save the time, server, name, type, and full response. Use a new record when you change networks or servers so that the conditions stay clear.

blocks.heading: Optional: a newer DNSSEC negative-response case
paragraphs: Compact Denial of Existence can reduce name disclosure with smaller denial proofs. Some nonexistent names receive a NODATA-like NOERROR reply with NXNAME in the NSEC or NSEC3 type bitmap. Read the DNSSEC proof and resolver behavior before deciding that the name exists.

In our example, the A reply already supplies an address, while the complete AAAA reply shows missing AAAA data. Keep both replies. For advanced cases, preserve the raw response and check it with tools that understand the mechanism. [RFC 9824](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9824/)

sections.heading: 5. Try one lookup in your own lab
paragraphs: Website supplement: these optional commands are separate from the made-up output above. Use a computer with dig and an authorized DNS lab server hosting your test zone. Agree on the target, record types, time, query volume, and stop conditions first.
192.0.2.53 is only an example DNS address. Replace it with your authorized host. These commands have not been run here, and your results are left for you to record.

blocks.heading: Preparation: check the tool
paragraphs: Run this in a Linux terminal. A version response confirms that dig is available. If it is missing, use your operating system’s package-management process; ask the administrator of a managed computer to handle installation.

Replace every sample IP and .test name with configured, authorized lab data. This page does not create a lab server, and no query was run here. [IPv4 documentation addresses](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5737) · [Reserved example names](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2606)

blocks.heading: In your local terminal, ask for one type at a time
paragraphs: The value after @ selects the server. A or AAAA selects the record type. Save the full response after each command before continuing.
blocks.code:
dig @192.0.2.53 www.example.test A
dig @192.0.2.53 www.example.test AAAA

blocks.heading: Read a made-up response first
paragraphs: This is a teaching excerpt with some header fields omitted, not a measured result. QUESTION is what was asked, ANSWER contains the data, and SERVER identifies the server queried. Save the full output in your own exercise.
blocks.code:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;www.example.test. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
www.example.test. 300 IN A 192.0.2.10
;; SERVER: 192.0.2.53#53

blocks.caption: Read one answer line
rows: www.example.test.: the record name; the final dot marks a fully qualified name.
300: the caching lifetime advertised in this reply, in seconds.

blocks.heading: Read the response, then write your observation
paragraphs: Find status and check that QUESTION contains the intended name and type. Review ANSWER, AUTHORITY, SERVER, query time, and TTL. Full output helps distinguish referrals from missing data.

If A returns an address and a complete reading of the AAAA response shows NODATA, record: “This server returned an IPv4 address and no AAAA data for this name in these queries.” To check website availability, test the corresponding web service within your authorization.
Keep a de-identified record when you finish. This exercise queries DNS; it requires no DNS configuration changes.

blocks.heading: Change the type to ask another question
paragraphs: Run and read one line at a time. Ask for NS, MX, TXT, and SOA at the zone name; ask for CNAME at an alias. Use -x for a reverse IP lookup. If data is absent, return to the full-response checks.

Without @, dig uses your computer’s configured DNS server. Keeping @ makes the lab server explicit. +noall +answer shows only the Answer section, which is useful after you have checked the full reply. Use full output when investigating failures. [ISC dig manual](https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/stable/manpages.html#dig-dns-lookup-utility)
blocks.code:
dig @192.0.2.53 shop.example.test CNAME
dig @192.0.2.53 example.test NS
dig @192.0.2.53 example.test MX
dig @192.0.2.53 example.test TXT
dig @192.0.2.53 example.test SOA
dig @192.0.2.53 -x 192.0.2.10

blocks.heading: Windows: query the same lab DNS server
paragraphs: Use Resolve-DnsName in PowerShell, or nslookup in Command Prompt or PowerShell. These are alternative tools; you do not need to repeat every query. -Server or the final address selects the DNS server. Record the same conditions despite the different output formats. [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/dnsclient/resolve-dnsname)
blocks.code:
Resolve-DnsName -Name www.example.test -Type A -Server 192.0.2.53 -DnsOnly
nslookup -type=A www.example.test 192.0.2.53
nslookup -type=MX example.test 192.0.2.53

sections.heading: 6. Manage a lookup and a zone copy separately
paragraphs: AXFR transfers the complete contents of one zone to another DNS server. Think of copying one zone’s address book. The full data of a delegated child zone is managed separately. [AXFR](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936)

Confirm authorization separately for ordinary queries and AXFR tests. This lesson explains transfers without probing third parties. Restrict transfer recipients, use appropriate authentication, and limit access to recursion and cached answers.

AXFR is a normal administrative function that transfers one zone over TCP. Broad access can expose names such as dev and backup in one response. Record those clues separately from reachability and vulnerability findings.

blocks.heading: Optional: settings to review in BIND
paragraphs: Review allow-transfer, allow-recursion, and allow-query-cache, and use authentication such as TSIG where appropriate. Check the installed version, configuration level, and effective settings. This lesson assumes no common default across all versions. [ISC BIND reference](https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference.html)

blocks.heading: Optional: cache clues and DNSSEC
paragraphs: Cache snooping uses cached responses to infer which names may have been queried. Shared caches and preloading affect those clues; attributing activity to a person requires other evidence.

DNSSEC uses signatures to support origin authentication and integrity checks. Keeping query contents private is a separate job. Signed zones using NSEC may also reveal relationships between names. Manage public records and access to resources separately. [DNSSEC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033)

sections.heading: 7. Authentic data and private transport solve different problems
paragraphs: DNSSEC lets validators check data origin and integrity using signatures. DoH and DoT protect a DNS transport connection; HTTPS protects HTTP traffic. Start by identifying which connection or data you need to protect.

blocks.caption: What each mechanism protects
rows: Authenticates DNS data and checks integrity. Encryption is handled separately.
Carries DNS over HTTPS, commonly on port 443, protecting the connection to the DNS endpoint.
Carries DNS over TLS, using TCP 853 by default, protecting that connection.
Protects HTTP traffic between a browser and a website or proxy. The service handles access rights.

blocks.heading: Optional: name clues and privacy limits
paragraphs: Traditional NSEC records reveal neighboring names and record types, which can support zone walking. Disclosure depends on how a zone is signed. Compact Denial can reduce those clues; a complete name list is not a universal DNSSEC property. [NSEC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4034) · [Compact Denial](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9824/)

DoH and DoT protect the transport to a DNS endpoint. That endpoint still processes the query; later connections and website permissions have their own protections. [DoH](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8484) · [DoT](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7858)

sections.heading: 8. Match each observation to the step you tested
paragraphs: After finding an address, choose the next test based on your question. This is a troubleshooting guide; one tool can cover several steps, and caches or proxies can change the actual path.

blocks.caption: From a name to access
blocks.description: Keep separate results for each step. A successful DNS lookup completes the name-resolution check.

items.title: DNS
items.body: Which records are returned? Use dig or nslookup.

items.title: Network
items.body: Can you connect to the specified IP and port within the agreed test scope?

items.title: TLS
items.body: Does TLS negotiation and certificate validation succeed?

items.title: HTTP
items.body: What status and content does the particular request return?

items.title: Access control
items.body: What can this identity do with this resource?

blocks.heading: Optional: compare DNS and a web request
paragraphs: The first line queries DNS. The second sends an HTTPS HEAD request from your terminal, involving resolution, a connection, TLS, and HTTP. Use a configured lab website with a trusted certificate, working local name resolution, and separate authorization for web testing.

curl uses its own resolution path; it does not inherit the @ server from dig. A site may restrict HEAD. Record the result for this request and investigate the stage that failed, keeping certificate verification enabled. [curl manual](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html)

blocks.caption: A record someone else can follow
rows: Time and timezone, network location, tool version, DNS server, name, and type.
Full response, status, sections, and TTL. Keep made-up examples separate from measured results.
The settings supported by this reply and questions that need a service test.

sections.heading: 9. Read in manageable parts
paragraphs: Start with one lookup you can explain, then explore management and security details as needed. P0/P1/P2 are teaching priorities for this lesson. The supplement’s 25–35 minute estimate is flexible; pause and resume within your available study time.

blocks.caption: Lesson priorities, not official exam weights
rows: Resolver roles; A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS; query tools; response interpretation.
Zones and AXFR; TTL, SOA, PTR, TXT; evidence and controls.
DNSSEC, NSEC, cache snooping, and transport protection.

sections.heading: 10. Teaching checks: answer before opening the explanation
paragraphs: Scenario Q5 (the original short check): the same DNS server returns 192.0.2.10 for www.example.test A, and a complete reading of its AAAA reply confirms ordinary NODATA. In one or two sentences, what have you confirmed, and what would you check to find out whether the website opens?

The four multiple-choice questions below and the scenario above are teaching exercises. Opening an explanation does not submit an answer or update your understanding status. Q&A awaits actual questions and discussion. The next core concept remains M04-03 FTP enumeration.

blocks.heading: Show the teaching explanation for Q5
paragraphs: Record that this DNS server returned an IPv4 address for the name and no AAAA data in these queries. To check the website, test the connection, TLS, and an actual HTTP request in the authorized lab. Check sign-in and action permissions separately.
This is a teaching explanation, not a submitted learner answer.

zh.prompt: DNS 查詢獲得一個 A 記錄，最合理的結論是？
options: 已證明網站可以正常開啟
已取得某個名稱對應的 IPv4 位址
已確認網站的登入權限
已取得伺服器管理權限
rationales: A：網站可用性由連線與應用程式測試確認。
B：正確，A 記錄提供名稱對應的 IPv4 位址。
C：登入權限由身分驗證與授權流程確認。
D：管理權限需要另有帳號與授權證據。

en.prompt: A DNS lookup returns an A record. What does that tell you?
options: The website is working.
An IPv4 address was returned for a name.
Website sign-in permissions are confirmed.
You have server administrator access.
rationales: A: Website availability needs connection and application tests.
B: Correct. An A record supplies an IPv4 address for a name.
C: Sign-in rights require authentication and authorization checks.
D: Administrative access requires separate account and permission evidence.

zh.prompt: 完整回應已確認為一般 NODATA（排除轉介及 Compact Denial 例外），查詢的是 AAAA。怎麼解讀？
options: 這個網域必定不存在
DNS 伺服器一定當機
該名稱存在，但沒有符合本次查詢類型的資料
這個網站已被入侵
rationales: A：一般 NODATA 與表示名稱不存在的 NXDOMAIN 要分開。
B：伺服器已回覆；運作狀態再依其他證據判斷。
C：正確，題目前提已確認為一般無該類型資料。
D：這筆回應描述 DNS 資料；入侵判斷需要其他證據。

en.prompt: The full AAAA reply is confirmed as ordinary NODATA, excluding referrals and the Compact Denial exception. How do you read it?
options: The domain must not exist.
The DNS server must be down.
The name exists, but this record type has no data.
The website has been compromised.
rationales: A: Ordinary NODATA differs from NXDOMAIN, which indicates a nonexistent name.
B: A reply arrived. Broader server health needs other evidence.
C: Correct. The question establishes the ordinary missing-type case.
D: This reply describes DNS data. Compromise requires other evidence.

zh.prompt: 為什麼 AXFR 需要存取控制？
options: 因為任何 DNS 查詢都會修改資料
因為 AXFR 可能傳送整個區域的資料
因為它能直接取得使用者密碼
因為它會自動開啟網站管理介面
rationales: A：本課一般查詢是讀取；動態更新是不同操作。
B：正確，需限定接收區域資料的對象並驗證授權。
C：AXFR 傳送區域記錄；密碼應保存在適當的秘密管理系統。
D：網站管理介面與其權限屬另一層服務。

en.prompt: Why does AXFR need access control?
options: Every DNS query modifies data.
AXFR can transfer an entire zone.
It directly retrieves user passwords.
It automatically opens a website administration panel.
rationales: A: The ordinary queries here read data; dynamic updates are separate operations.
B: Correct. Limit and authenticate the recipients of zone data.
C: AXFR transfers zone records; passwords belong in appropriate secret storage.
D: Website administration and its permissions are a separate service layer.

zh.prompt: DNSSEC 的核心安全功能是哪一項？
options: 隱藏所有 DNS 名稱
加密所有網站的 HTTPS 流量
驗證 DNS 資料來源與完整性
阻止任何人查詢公開的 A 記錄
rationales: A：DNSSEC 處理可驗證性；名稱揭露另有設計考量。
B：HTTPS 流量由 TLS 等機制保護。
C：正確，驗證端使用 DNSSEC 簽章與信任鏈檢查資料。
D：公開查詢政策與 DNSSEC 簽署分開管理。

en.prompt: What is the core security function of DNSSEC?
options: Hide all DNS names.
Encrypt every website’s HTTPS traffic.
Authenticate DNS data origin and check integrity.
Block everyone from querying public A records.
rationales: A: DNSSEC provides verifiability; name disclosure is a separate design concern.
B: TLS protects HTTPS traffic.
C: Correct. Validators use DNSSEC signatures and a chain of trust to check data.
D: Public query policy is managed separately from DNSSEC signing.
